## Root cause

The failure isn't in `routes/public.map` itself — the map file correctly lists a specific `/health` entry ahead of the `/*` wildcard entry, and it's not being parsed at all in this code path.

The actual bug is in **`router/routes.go`**:

```go
func HealthHandler() string { return "wildcard" }
```

`HealthHandler()` is hardcoded to return `"wildcard"` instead of `"health"`. This is a source-level regression — the handler simply returns the wrong constant, unconditionally, regardless of routing logic. The test `TestHealthRoute` in `router/routes_test.go` expects `HealthHandler()` to return `"health"`, but gets `"wildcard"`, producing the failure message `"shadowed by wildcard"`.

So the fix belongs in `router/routes.go` (changing the return value to `"health"`), not in `routes/public.map`, which is already correctly configured.
